newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO to meet Israelis, doubts restart of talks.
newsitem.headline: PLO to meet Israelis, doubts restart of talks.

text.p: Palestinian officials will attend a meeting with Israelis now being arranged by U.S. envoy Dennis Ross but doubt it will lead to a resumption of peace talks, PLO officials said on Monday.

Ross met with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in the West Bank city of Ramallah on Sunday night to try to arrange a PLO-Israeli meeting to discuss the two-month-old freeze in negotiations, PLO officials said.

"We will attend the meeting. Two Palestinian negotiators will be named to this informal meeting which may take place in the coming few days to discuss, but we doubt it will lead to resumption of negotiations," a PLO official said.
The official, who insisted on anonymity said the proposed meeting, which would take place at the U.S. ambassador's house in Tel Aviv, "was simply an attempt to resume contacts, not negotiations".
"It is an attempt to discuss the issues that led to the freeze in peace talks, not to resolve the problems," he said.
PLO officials agreed with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's assessment on Sunday that it would take some time before the U.S. envoy would get the sides to talk peace again.
"Without a freeze on settlement activities, the Palestinians will not resume the talks," another PLO official said.
Talks were halted in March when Israel broke ground at a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, occupied by Israel in 1967 and later annexed.

The fate of Jerusalem is up for negotiations in final status talks. Palestinians want East Jerusalem as the capital of a future Palestinian state while Israel insists it is part of its united capital.

Netanyahu said on Sunday, while Ross and Arafat were meeting, he was proud of his March decision that sent bulldozers to carve out a new Jewish settlement in Arab Jerusalem, plunging peacemaking between the sides into deep crisis.
PLO officials criticised the U.S. for its refusal to press Israel to halt settlement activities in Palestinian areas during mediation to restart the talks.
They said without direct American pressure on Israel to stop building, a meeting of Palestinians and Israelis would be ineffective.
But Israel's government spokesman Moshe Fogel said Israel would continue to build settlements.
Officials said Ross, scheduled to meet King Hussein in Jordan on Monday, is expected to return to Jerusalem later in the day to resume efforts to arrange the meeting.

PLO and Israeli officials are at odds over the issues to be discussed at the meeting. Palestinians want to discuss settlements and Israeli violations in Jerusalem while Israelis want to raise the issues of fighting "terror" and Palestinian violations of peace deals.
Top PLO negotiator Saeb Erekat told Reuters he handed Ross a list of 1,300 Palestinian homes Israel wants to demolish in parts of the West Bank still under Israeli control.

"During the past three months, Israel handed 1,300 notifications to Palestinians in parts of the West Bank still under occupation ordering them to evacuate their homes before they are demolished," Erekat said.
"I handed that list to Ross and told him that seven homes have already been demolished last week. These are only a fraction of Israeli violations of the accords," he said.
